title: JPA Repository Queries
summary: Add derived queries, declared JPQL queries and bounded results.

richText: A derived query is a query Spring Data builds from a repository method name.
The method names use entity property names, not database column names.
findByDepartment searches the department property. And and Or combine conditions.
A misspelled property can prevent the repository from being created.

example.title: Find employees by department
description: Use the Employee entity and database connection from the preceding lessons.
explanation: Spring Data derives a query for the department property.
Calling findByDepartment("Engineering") returns employees whose department matches Engineering.
A query returning List returns an empty list when no rows match.

richText: Use @Query when the query is clearer than a long method name.
JPQL is the JPA query language. It uses entity names and properties.
Native SQL uses database tables and columns. Set nativeQuery=true when using SQL with @Query.
Bind user-supplied values as parameters. Do not construct a query by joining raw input into its text.

description: This is an alternative EmployeeRepository declaration. Use it instead of the derived-query declaration above.
explanation: Employee is the entity name. department is its Java property.
The named parameter receives the method argument.
The persistence provider translates JPQL into SQL for the configured database.

richText: Pageable supplies a page number, page size and sort order. Page numbers start at zero.
Page includes the rows and total-count information. Calculating the total can require a separate count query.
Slice reports whether another slice exists without requiring the same total-count calculation.
Use a stable sort. Add a unique property such as id when other sort values can repeat.
